english.title: Assist arrival / entry / remain in United Kingdom in breach of exclusion order - immigration
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), which assisted **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to

(A)_[arrive in]_
(B)_[attempt to arrive in]_
(C)_[enter]_
(D)_[attempt to enter]_
(E)_[remain in]_
(F)_[attempt to remain in]_

the United Kingdom, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the act so assisted that person and knowing or having reasonable cause for believing that the Secretary of State had made an order excluding that person from the United Kingdom on the grounds of public policy, public security or public health
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 25B(3) and 25(6) of the Immigration Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
did an act assisting individual to arrive in/enter into/remain in UK
knowing/having reasonable cause to believe it would so assist
knowing/having reasonable cause for believing the Secretary of State
had made exclusion order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) As substituted by section 143 of the Nationality, Immigration and Asylum Act 2002 as from 10/02/03.
(ii) Options (B), (D) and (F), inserted by paragraph 4 of Schedule 14 to the Immigration Act 2016 on 31 May 2016. These options should not be used in relation to incidents occurring prior to this date.
(iii) This offence is not committed when the order in force is a 'Temporary Exclusion Order', as defined in section 24B(5).
(iv) Section 25B is repealed from 23:00 on 31st December 2020.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
